passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: It is within the power of all in every Church to contemplate the tradition of the apostles manifested throughout the whole world and to reckon up those who were instituted bishops by the apostles and their succession to our own times; those who taught nothing like what the heretics rave about.

source.title: Against Heresies
source.author: Irenaeus of Lyons
source.notes: Five-book refutation of Gnosticism; ANF Vol. 1 translation by Roberts and Rambaut, revised for New Advent by Kevin Knight.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: The tradition derived from the apostles of the very great, very ancient, universally known Church founded at Rome by Peter and Paul — every Church must agree with this Church on account of its preeminent authority (potiorem principalitatem); the faith preached to men comes down to our time by means of the successions of the bishops.

source.title: Against Heresies
source.author: Irenaeus of Lyons
source.notes: Five-book refutation of Gnosticism; ANF Vol. 1 translation by Roberts and Rambaut, revised for New Advent by Kevin Knight.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: The Rome bishop succession: Peter and Paul committed the episcopate to Linus; then Anacletus; then Clement (third from the apostles, who had seen the blessed apostles); then Evaristus, Alexander, Sixtus, Telephorus (gloriously martyred), Hyginus, Pius, Anicetus, Soter, and Eleutherius (twelfth from the apostles, now in office). In this order and by this succession the ecclesiastical tradition from the apostles and the preaching of the truth have come down to us.
